note: Four p38-alpha inhibitors reached COPD patients on rodent LPS/endotoxin and human-cell PD models that translated cleanly to healthy-volunteer inhaled-LPS challenge (sputum neutrophils and TNF-alpha fell for PH-797804, PF-03715455 and AZD7624), but oral PH-797804's 6-week FEV1 win shrank to 27-60 mL in two 12-week trials and was dropped, inhaled AZD7624 failed on exacerbations (HR 1.39), acumapimod missed its FEV1 primary in both exacerbation trials, and PF-03715455's COPD trial was stopped at 13 patients; losmapimod and dilmapimod are not members and are not scored.
label: COPD (p38 inhibitors)

engagement.model: Rat and cynomolgus endotoxin-induced TNF-alpha PD model (PH-797804)
engagement.note: PH-797804 blocked systemic endotoxin-induced TNF in rat and monkey; in human endotoxin studies it cut TNF-alpha and IL-6 dose-dependently, paralleling p38 inhibition.
engagement.short: Human endotoxin TNF fell as rat predicted
engagement.quote: Finally, PH-797804 reduced tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-6 production in clinical studies after endotoxin administration in a dose-dependent manner, paralleling inhibition of the target enzyme.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Hope 2009 (JPET 331:882, PMID 19720877); the human endotoxin numbers are in the full text, which was not read. Healthy volunteers, not COPD patients; the same system is scored under the same model_id in the osteoarthritis tile.
engagement.judgement: Scored same because the source itself puts the rat/monkey endotoxin PD data beside the human endotoxin study and reports the same dose-dependent TNF inhibition (comparison_stated true). Readout is downstream (cytokine output after a systemic stimulus), not p38 occupancy. Magnitude direction-only because the abstract gives no human numbers.
engagement.magnitude_basis: endotoxin-induced TNF-alpha inhibition (abstract reports direction and dose-dependence only)

engagement.note: Opening entry: sibling p38 inhibitor SB 239063 cut BAL neutrophils, IL-6 and MMP-9 after inhaled LPS at 3-30 mg/kg; no member drug and no human PD readout yet.
engagement.short: Rodent LPS neutrophilia model, sibling drug
engagement.quote: Airway neutrophil infiltration and interleukin (IL)-6 levels, assessed by bronchoalveolar lavage 48 h after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation, were inhibited dose dependently by 3-30 mg/kg of SB 239063 given orally twice a day.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Am J Physiol Lung 279:L895, PMID 11053025); the species of the inhaled-LPS arm is not stated in the abstract (guinea-pig alveolar macrophages and rat bleomycin fibrosis are named for the other arms). Medicherla 2008 (doi 10.1124/jpet.107.127092, SD-282 in an 11-day mouse tobacco-smoke model) makes the same class prediction and is not scored as a separate track.
engagement.judgement: Opens the class-level COPD-aspect track at its first published use (2000) with a non-member p38 inhibitor (product_in_model false), which the brief allows as a sibling-drug prediction. Whether PF-03715455 or AZD7624 were later run in a rodent LPS model is in paywalled full texts (Millan 2011, Pehrson 2018) that were not read.

engagement.note: Single doses of oral PH-797804 30 mg and inhaled PF-03715455 20 mg cut post-LPS sputum neutrophil percentage by 15.1-15.3 and 8.0 points in healthy volunteers; fluticasone did nothing.
engagement.short: Human LPS neutrophils fell as rodent predicted
engagement.quote: The p38 MAPK inhibitors PH-797804 and PF-03715455 both reduced neutrophilic airway inflammation after LPS challenge in healthy subjects.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4564450; Eur J Clin Pharmacol 71:1175, epub 2015-08-13). Three crossover studies NCT02084485, NCT01314885, NCT01364519; no registry results posted. Healthy volunteers, not COPD patients; PH-797804's LPS study ran 2006-2008 but was first public here.
engagement.reason: Human LPS neutrophils fell as rodent predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): model side Underwood 2000 (sibling SB 239063 cut BAL neutrophils after inhaled LPS), patient side the same readout (sputum neutrophils after inhaled LPS) falling in dosed volunteers on two member drugs. Readout tier downstream: cell influx after a stimulus, not p38 occupancy. Magnitude direction-only because % BAL inhibition in a rodent and an 8-15 percentage-point sputum change (about 25-50% of the LPS response) are not commensurable. AZD7624's 56.6% neutrophil and 85.4% TNF-alpha reduction (Patel 2018) is scored on its own track.
engagement.magnitude_basis: post-LPS sputum neutrophil percentage change (-15.1/-15.3 points PH-797804, -8.0 points PF-03715455) against rodent % BAL neutrophil inhibition; not commensurable

engagement.model: AstraZeneca human alveolar-macrophage/whole-blood LPS-TNF potency model with rat inhaled lung PK (AZD7624)
engagement.note: AZD7624's unbound LPS-TNF potency in vitro (pIC50u 8.4-9.0) matched ex-vivo whole blood from dosed volunteers (8.8), and inhaled dosing cut LPS-induced sputum TNF-alpha 85% at 0.3 nM unbound plasma.
engagement.short: Ex-vivo potency matched; sputum TNF fell 85%
engagement.quote: The pIC50u in whole blood ex vivo was 8.8, showing good in vitro/in vivo potency correlations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Pehrson 2018 (JPET 365:567, epub 2018-03-16, PMID 29549158); the human LPS-challenge trial is NCT01937338 (no registry results). Healthy volunteers, not COPD patients. The in vitro/rat work predates the 2013 first-in-human study but was first public in 2018, so model_first_use_year 2013 is a proxy.
engagement.reason: Ex-vivo whole-blood potency matched in vitro
engagement.judgement: Scored same because the source itself puts the in vitro human-cell potencies and rat lung PK beside the human ex-vivo and sputum PD results (comparison_stated true). Readout tier direct: ex-vivo blockade of an LPS stimulus in blood from dosed subjects; the sputum TNF-alpha fall is the downstream confirmation. Magnitude within 2x on the quantity the paper compares (in vitro whole-blood pIC50u 8.7 vs ex vivo 8.8).
engagement.magnitude_basis: unbound pIC50 for LPS-induced TNF-alpha: human whole blood in vitro 8.7 vs ex vivo after inhaled dosing 8.8

engagement.model: Ex-vivo COPD-patient alveolar macrophages, LPS cytokine release (SB239063, SD-282; later AZD7624)
engagement.note: Macrophages from smokers and emphysema patients: sibling p38 inhibitors cut LPS-induced TNF-alpha regardless of disease status; AZD7624 was run in the same system (Higham 2018) but no dosed-patient sputum readout was ever taken.
engagement.short: COPD-cell readout never measured in dosed patients
engagement.quote: Thus, inhibition of macrophage cytokine production may have therapeutic benefit.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Br J Pharmacol 149:393, PMC1978438). Higham 2018 (doi 10.2147/COPD.S159936) ran AZD7624 on alveolar macrophages, PBMCs and bronchial epithelial cells from COPD frequent and infrequent exacerbators; Patel 2018 states the COPD trial collected no sputum biomarkers, so the model's readout was never compared in treated patients.
engagement.reason: Never compared in dosed COPD patients
engagement.judgement: Untested rather than empty: the ex-vivo patient-cell system existed from 2006, a member drug was run in it in 2018, and nobody measured its readout in dosed COPD patients. Not scored at patient level either, because Higham 2018 found exacerbation frequency did not change the response and no trial stratified on it.

dose.model: Rat and cynomolgus endotoxin-induced TNF-alpha PD model (PH-797804)
dose.note: Hope 2009 projected human doses from the rat/monkey PD-exposure relationship; no COPD dose had been tested against it yet.
dose.quote: In addition, a direct correspondence between p38 MAP kinase inhibition and anti-inflammatory activity was observed with PH-797804, thus providing confidence in dose projections for further human studies in chronic inflammatory disease.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the projected exposure target is in the full text, which was not read.

dose.model: Rat and cynomolgus endotoxin-induced TNF-alpha PD model (PH-797804)
dose.note: Once-daily 0.5-10 mg for 6 weeks in 230 COPD patients: 3 and 6 mg raised trough FEV1 86-93 mL over placebo and were tolerated, so the projected dose range was reached and worked.
dose.short: 3-6 mg reached target and raised FEV1
dose.quote: PH-797804 showed a statistically significant improvement in trough FEV1 at week 6 compared with placebo of 0.086 litre (95% Bayesian CI 0.008 to 0.164) and 0.093 litre (95% CI 0.018 to 0·166) at 3 and 6 mg PH-797804, respectively.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Thorax 68:738, epub 2013-03-28; full text paywalled). NCT00559910 has no registry results. Whether the 3-6 mg doses match Hope 2009's projected exposure is in two paywalled full texts, so the match is inferred from the dose range tested.
dose.judgement: Dose is tied to efficacy: the model's exposure range was reached (0.5-10 mg tested) and the 6-week primary endpoint responded at 3-6 mg, so same. No tolerability margin was published for the model (margin_stated false), so the dose-related adverse-event discontinuations seen later are not a decision-16 case.
dose.magnitude_basis: trough FEV1 response at 3-6 mg once daily; the model's projected human exposure was not read

dose.model: AstraZeneca human alveolar-macrophage/whole-blood LPS-TNF potency model with rat inhaled lung PK (AZD7624)
dose.note: A 1.2 mg lung-deposited dose cut LPS-induced sputum TNF-alpha 85% at sub-pharmacologic plasma levels, yet 1.0 mg once daily for 12 weeks in 213 frequent exacerbators did nothing; AZD7624 was dropped.
dose.short: Lung PD target hit in volunteers
dose.quote: However, AZD7624 failed to provide any benefit in a 3 month COPD exacerbation study.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5877500; epub 2018-03-27); NCT02238483 results posted 2018-04-18 (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.81-2.40, p=0.2371). The exposure target (pIC50u) and the rat lung:plasma ratio come from Pehrson 2018 (abstract-level).
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction (rule v4): the lung PD target was shown reached in volunteers. Reached, failed, abandoned: the model's lung PD target was shown reached in volunteers (85% sputum TNF-alpha inhibition) and the exacerbation trial at a similar dose failed, so contra with derived_from efficacy. The 12-week trial measured no sputum PD, so whether the lung target held in patients over 12 weeks is not known; the challenge dose (1,200 ug lung-deposited) and trial dose (1.0 mg delivered) are also not identical.

dose.model: BCT197 population PK-PD tolerance model (healthy-volunteer ex-vivo LPS TNF-alpha)
dose.note: Novartis' PK-PD model of acumapimod found TNF suppression wearing off under continuous exposure and predicted intermittent dosing would do better; neither COPD trial included a continuous-dosing arm to test it.
dose.quote: Simulations of posology dependence in drug effect suggest that an intermittent regimen may offer clinical benefit over continuous dosing and limit the impact of tolerance development.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 4:691, PMC4759708, epub 2015-11-09). The single- and two-dose regimens of NCT01332097 (run 2011-2013) and NCT02700919 (2016-2017) are consistent with the prediction but no trial compared them with daily dosing, so the regimen target cannot be scored.
dose.judgement: Untested: an in-silico model exists for a member drug and made a regimen prediction, but no admissible comparison exists because both acumapimod trials used only single or repeated single doses. Not treated as a retrodiction of NCT01332097's design, since that trial's results were not public until 2019.

dose.model: Acumapimod PBPK drug-drug-interaction model (CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors; healthy-volunteer DDI studies MBCT102/MBCT103)
dose.note: Mereo built a PBPK model of acumapimod after the azithromycin DDI study (Oct 2016) to predict exposure under moderate and strong CYP3A4 inhibition before any such study was run.
dose.short: PBPK DDI exposure prediction not yet tested
dose.quote: Consequently, a physiologically-based PK (PBPK) model was developed to predict how co-administration of a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor with acumapimod affects acumapimod systemic exposure, to inform decision making and increase confidence that toxicity margins would not be exceeded.
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 10:30, PMC7825188, received 2020-04-08, epub 2020-12-30). First-use year 2017 is a proxy: the paper says the model was verified on study MBCT102 (NCT02926326, completed Oct 2016) and applied prospectively before MBCT103 began (2018-03-19). Quote normalises the source's non-breaking hyphens.
dose.judgement: Opens a separate in-silico track: a PBPK DDI model is a different model from De Buck 2015's population PK-PD tolerance model (bct197-pkpd-tolerance-insilico) and makes a different prediction (exposure under CYP3A4 inhibition, not TNF-alpha tolerance), so it gets its own model_id.

dose.model: Acumapimod PBPK drug-drug-interaction model (CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors; healthy-volunteer DDI studies MBCT102/MBCT103)
dose.note: Model predicted itraconazole would raise acumapimod AUC 1.31-1.69x with Cmax unchanged and stay inside the safety margin; MBCT103 (16 healthy men) observed AUC +10%, Cmax unchanged, no safety findings.
dose.short: Itraconazole exposure within predicted, tolerated range
dose.quote: Accuracy of the PBPK model predictions was confirmed by the MBCT103 study results, which indicated that itraconazole had no meaningful effect on the acumapimod PKs.
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The model over-predicted the AUC ratio (1.31 model 1 / 1.69 model 2 vs observed 1.10; the authors note the predicted AUC CI fell outside the 80-125% window) while the Cmax ratio (1.03 vs 1.00) was exact; the authors still call the prediction confirmed. MBCT103 is NCT03498170 (first posted 2018-04-13, no results posted), so the paper is the only public record of the comparison. The verapamil prediction (AUC 1.13-1.27x) was never tested clinically. Healthy volunteers, not COPD patients.
dose.judgement: Scored in the dose cell as 'same': the source itself sets the prospective PBPK prediction beside the observed healthy-volunteer exposure (comparison_stated true), the exposure stayed inside the model's stated toxicity margin and the drug was tolerated, which is decision 16's margin_stated case. Magnitude within_2x on the AUC geometric-mean ratio (predicted 1.31-1.69 vs observed 1.10). Healthy-volunteer PK counts under the dose rule. This does not score efficacy: the model says nothing about whether the exposure is enough.
dose.magnitude_basis: acumapimod AUC0-inf geometric-mean ratio with itraconazole: predicted 1.31 (model 1) / 1.69 (model 2) vs observed 1.10; Cmax ratio predicted 1.03 vs observed 1.00
dose.reason: PBPK DDI prediction held in volunteers

efficacy.note: Sibling SB 239063 cut LPS-induced BAL neutrophils, IL-6 (>90%) and MMP-9 (64%) and bleomycin fibrosis; the authors read this as therapeutic potential in chronic airway disease.
efficacy.short: Sibling p38 inhibitor blocks LPS lung neutrophilia
efficacy.quote: Therefore, SB 239063 demonstrates activity against a range of sequelae commonly associated with COPD and fibrosis, supporting the therapeutic potential of p38 MAPK inhibitors such as SB 239063 in chronic airway disease.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no member drug was in this model and the model measured inflammatory readouts, never lung function.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the earliest published COPD-aspect model prediction for the class used a non-member inhibitor (product_in_model false). No member had a COPD patient result yet.

efficacy.note: Oral PH-797804 3 and 6 mg met the 6-week trough-FEV1 primary endpoint (+86 and +93 mL vs placebo) in 230 moderate-to-severe COPD patients and improved dyspnoea.
efficacy.quote: PH-797804 showed a statistically significant improvement in trough FEV1 at week 6 compared with placebo of 0.086 litre (95% Bayesian CI 0.008 to 0.164) and 0.093 litre (95% CI 0.018 to 0·166) at 3 and 6 mg PH-797804, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Thorax 68:738, epub 2013-03-28, PMID 23539534); NCT00559910 has no registry results. An adaptive-design 6-week trial with Bayesian CIs, not a conventional Phase 2b; the 10 mg arm is not reported as significant in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): model side Underwood 2000, patient side the PH-797804 primary endpoint. Same in direction only: the model read BAL neutrophils and cytokines, the trial trough FEV1, so magnitude is direction_only. Losmapimod's contemporaneous COPD trials are not members and are set aside.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: trough FEV1 change vs placebo against rodent % inhibition of BAL neutrophils; not commensurable

patient_trials.quote: PH-797804 3 mg and 6 mg showed an improvement in the baseline dyspnoea index/transition dyspnoea index total focal score at week 6.

efficacy.note: Two 12-week trials (377 patients on ICS/LABA, 721 on tiotropium) gave only 27-60 mL trough FEV1 over placebo; neither met Pfizer's predefined criteria and PH-797804 was abandoned.
efficacy.quote: However, none of the 5 doses of PH-797804 met the predefined decision criteria for improvement over placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 at Week 12.
efficacy.confidence_note: EudraCT results for NCT01543919 (first published 2015-07-11) read directly; the ICS/LABA-background trial NCT01321463 is in the Pfizer public-disclosure synopsis attached to EudraCT 2010-024219-15 (published 2016-06-02; 27 mL, posterior probability 0.104 of a 50 mL gain). The point estimates were positive with CIs excluding zero, so this is a failure against the sponsor's 50 mL bar rather than a null effect; the call could be argued as partial.
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra under 'reached, failed, abandoned': the primary endpoint in two adequately sized 12-week trials fell below the predefined decision criteria (32-60 mL and 27 mL vs a 50 mL requirement) and the program ended, so the 6-week win did not hold. Judged on the data, not the sponsor's words: a 27-60 mL FEV1 gain is below the ~100 mL minimal important difference. One drug's contra beats another's same on the track.

patient_trials.quote: However, none of the 5 doses of PH-797804 met the predefined decision criteria for improvement over placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 at Week 12.

However, PH-797804 did not meet the second predefined decision criteria of a >0.50 posterior probability of a ≥0.050 L change from Baseline in trough FEV1 over placebo at Week 12 (estimated posterior probability of 0.104).

efficacy.note: Inhaled AZD7624 1.0 mg daily for 12 weeks in 213 frequent exacerbators on ICS/LABA: no effect on time to first exacerbation (HR 1.39), FEV1, SGRQ or symptoms.
efficacy.quote: In the 213 patients randomized into the Proof of Principle study, there was no statistically significant difference between AZD7624 and placebo when comparing the number of days to the first moderate or severe exacerbation or early dropout.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5877500, epub 2018-03-27); NCT02238483 results posted 2018-04-18 (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.81-2.40, p=0.2371). Single-dose, exacerbation-based Phase 2a after an oral-steroid run-in.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the class-level contra with a second member on a different endpoint and route: the rodent model predicts airway anti-inflammatory activity and the inhaled drug, selected to maximise lung p38 inhibition, gave no clinical benefit. Paired with Underwood 2000; AZD7624's own stated comparisons are on the human-LPS-challenge and AstraZeneca cell-model tracks.

patient_trials.quote: Primary results No statistically significant difference between AZD7624 and placebo was observed when comparing the number of days to the first ExDo event (HR =1.39, 95% CI 0.81, 2.40) ( Figure 3A ).

efficacy.note: Oral acumapimod in 183 patients with acute exacerbations missed its Day-10 FEV1 primary (p=0.082); the 282-patient AETHER repeat also missed Day-7 FEV1 vs placebo (+27 and +58 mL, p=0.51 and 0.15).
efficacy.quote: Although the primary endpoint (FEV1 at Day 10) was not met (p = 0.082), there was a significant improvement in FEV1 with acumapimod repeat-dose 75 mg versus placebo at Day 8 (p = 0.022)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (COPD 16:344, epub 2019-11-04, PMID 31682162); the quote is the first part of the sentence, which continues 'which, though not a prespecified endpoint, was part of an overall trend.' NCT01332097 results posted 2023-03-21 (Day-10 LS mean differences vs placebo -72 to +124 mL, all CIs crossing zero). AETHER NCT02700919 results posted 2020-11-30 (tier 3) post-date this entry and change no status.
efficacy.reason: Three members failed; 6-week win did not hold
efficacy.judgement: Third member failure on the class track, in acute exacerbations rather than stable COPD: the primary endpoint was not met in the Novartis trial and, per the registry record, not met against placebo in Mereo's AETHER either. Acumapimod has no published disease-model data, so the pairing is with the class-level rodent model (product_in_model false).

patient_trials.quote: Change in FEV1 From Baseline to Day 5 or Baseline to Day 10 Measure: FEV1 Change in Forced Expiry Volume in 1 Second
Change From Baseline in FEV1 to Day 7 - ITT Population

efficacy.model: Healthy-volunteer inhaled-LPS sputum neutrophilia challenge (PH-797804, PF-03715455, AZD7624)
efficacy.note: Opening entry: Pfizer ran PH-797804 through a single-dose inhaled-LPS sputum challenge in healthy volunteers in 2006-2008; the result stayed unpublished until 2015.
efficacy.short: LPS challenge run before COPD trials, unpublished
efficacy.quote: PH-797804 LPS Study in Healthy Volunteers
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record only (first posted 2014-03-12, study dates 2006-09 to 2008-03, no results); the quote is the record's brief title. Dated to the study start as the model's first use, a proxy.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the human-challenge track at its first use so the strip shows the model existed seven years before a COPD comparison was public. model_kind human_challenge; the challenge is itself the human PD readout, so this track has no engagement cell.

efficacy.model: Healthy-volunteer inhaled-LPS sputum neutrophilia challenge (PH-797804, PF-03715455, AZD7624)
efficacy.note: Singh 2015 set the challenge result (PH-797804 cut post-LPS sputum neutrophils 15 points) beside the 93 mL 6-week FEV1 gain in COPD patients as a translation of the model.
efficacy.short: LPS-challenge win paired with 6-week FEV1 win
efficacy.quote: It has been shown that PH-797804 improves FEV1 by 93 mL in COPD patients treated for 6 weeks
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4564450, epub 2015-08-13); the quote normalises the subscript 'FEV 1' and drops the trailing citation bracket. By this date the 12-week EudraCT failure (2015-07-11) was already public and is not cited by the paper, so the stated match rests on the 6-week trial only; the track turns contra in 2018.
efficacy.judgement: Scored same because the source itself places the challenge-model result and the COPD trial result side by side (comparison_stated true), in direction only. Not a retrodiction: the challenge study was run in 2006-2008, before the COPD trial, and merely published late. PF-03715455 also cut sputum neutrophils (8 points) here but its COPD trial (NCT02366637) was stopped at 13 patients and cannot score.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: 6-week trough FEV1 gain (93 mL) against a 15-point fall in post-LPS sputum neutrophil percentage; not commensurable

patient_trials.quote: PH-797804 showed a statistically significant improvement in trough FEV1 at week 6 compared with placebo of 0.086 litre (95% Bayesian CI 0.008 to 0.164) and 0.093 litre (95% CI 0.018 to 0·166) at 3 and 6 mg PH-797804, respectively.

efficacy.model: Healthy-volunteer inhaled-LPS sputum neutrophilia challenge (PH-797804, PF-03715455, AZD7624)
efficacy.note: AZD7624 cut LPS-induced sputum neutrophils 56.6% and TNF-alpha 85.4% in volunteers, then gave no exacerbation, FEV1 or symptom benefit in 213 COPD patients; the authors call the challenge a poor predictor.
efficacy.short: LPS challenge called a poor COPD predictor
efficacy.quote: Although LPS challenge has been proposed as a model of airway inflammation that can be used to evaluate drugs for COPD, our results demonstrate the limited value of LPS challenge in predicting the benefit for COPD.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5877500, epub 2018-03-27); challenge study NCT01937338 (no registry results), COPD trial NCT02238483 (results 2018-04-18). The paper also notes the CRP/IL-6/MIP-1beta falls seen after LPS were not reproduced in COPD patients.
efficacy.judgement: Stated miss (comparison_stated true, source_calls_it miss): the model's own authors conclude the challenge did not predict COPD benefit. Contra beats the 2015 same on this track; no later source shows the patient signal reversed. PF-03715455's 4-week COPD crossover (NCT02366637, terminated for business reasons at n=13, results 2016-07-06: -47 mL vs +80 mL on placebo in 6 completers) is listed but too small to score.

patient_trials.quote: Time to First Moderate to Severe COPD Exacerbation or Early Drop-out Related to Worsening of COPD Symptoms
Study terminated on 7 April 2015 for business reasons. No safety and/or efficacy concerns contributed to the termination of the study

efficacy.model: AstraZeneca human alveolar-macrophage/whole-blood LPS-TNF potency model with rat inhaled lung PK (AZD7624)
efficacy.note: AZD7624 blocked LPS-induced TNF-alpha and IL-6 in human alveolar macrophages (pIC50 9.2) and p38-alpha was the isoform raised in COPD lung, yet the 12-week exacerbation trial showed no benefit on any endpoint.
efficacy.short: In-vitro cytokine block, no exacerbation benefit
efficacy.quote: Furthermore, AZD7624 decreased LPS-stimulated cytokine release in human alveolar macrophages in vitro, and decreased systemic and lung inflammatory markers after inhaled LPS challenge. However, AZD7624 failed to provide any benefit in a 3 month COPD exacerbation study.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5877500); two consecutive sentences from the Discussion. The in situ proximity-ligation isoform work on COPD lung tissue is in the same paper.
efficacy.reason: Cell model right on PD, wrong on benefit
efficacy.judgement: Stated miss on AstraZeneca's own track (comparison_stated true): the paper sets the in vitro and challenge results beside the trial failure. Scored separately from the human-challenge track because the cell system is a different model, and from the rodent track because AZD7624 was never reported in a rodent LPS model.

patient_trials.quote: As detailed in Table 3 , there was no statistically significant difference in change from baseline comparing the AZD7624 and placebo arms with respect to FEV 1 , FVC, quality of life (SGRQ-C), dyspnea index (TDI), symptoms (as defined by EXACT E-RS), use of reliever medications, or night-time awakenings.

efficacy.model: Mouse tobacco-smoke airway-inflammation model (SD-282 in A/J mice; later SB203580 in C57BL/6)
efficacy.note: Sibling p38alpha inhibitor SD-282 cut smoke-induced BAL macrophages, neutrophils, COX-2 and IL-6 in an 11-day A/J mouse model where dexamethasone failed; no member drug was ever reported in this model.
efficacy.short: Smoke-model prediction, no member drug tested
efficacy.quote: This is the first evidence that a p38α-selective MAPK inhibitor can exert pulmonary anti-inflammatory activity in a TS exposure model when given in a therapeutic mode, establishing the potential of p38 MAPK inhibitors as a therapy for COPD.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (JPET 324:921, PMID 18056868, epub 2007-12-04, print 2008); PubMed renders the Greek as 'p38alpha'. Lee 2014 (doi 10.1186/1471-2466-14-79, SB203580 in C57BL/6 acute smoke exposure) is the same system with another sibling. No public source puts PH-797804, AZD7624, PF-03715455 or acumapimod in a smoke model, so product_in_model is false throughout.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the canonical COPD disease model as its own track, at its first use with a p38 inhibitor (2007 epub). It is a different system from the rodent inhaled-LPS neutrophilia model (chronic smoke exposure with steroid-insensitive inflammation vs an acute endotoxin stimulus) and its prediction is disease-level, so a separate model_id. Sibling-only, as the brief allows.

efficacy.model: Mouse tobacco-smoke airway-inflammation model (SD-282 in A/J mice; later SB203580 in C57BL/6)
efficacy.note: First member result in COPD patients: oral PH-797804 3 and 6 mg beat placebo on trough FEV1 at week 6 (+86 and +93 mL), the direction the smoke model predicted for a p38 inhibitor.
efficacy.quote: PH-797804 showed a statistically significant improvement in trough FEV1 at week 6 compared with placebo of 0.086 litre (95% Bayesian CI 0.008 to 0.164) and 0.093 litre (95% CI 0.018 to 0·166) at 3 and 6 mg PH-797804, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Thorax 68:738, epub 2013-03-28, PMID 23539534); NCT00559910 has no registry results. The model read BAL cell counts in smoke-exposed mice, the trial read trough FEV1 in stable COPD without ICS, so only direction is comparable.
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): model side Medicherla 2008 (sibling SD-282, product_in_model false), patient side the first member-drug primary endpoint in COPD. Same in direction only, as the draft's rodent-LPS track scores the same trial.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: trough FEV1 vs placebo at week 6 against % inhibition of smoke-induced BAL cell influx; not commensurable

patient_trials.quote: PH-797804 3 mg and 6 mg showed an improvement in the baseline dyspnoea index/transition dyspnoea index total focal score at week 6.

efficacy.model: Mouse tobacco-smoke airway-inflammation model (SD-282 in A/J mice; later SB203580 in C57BL/6)
efficacy.note: PH-797804's two 12-week trials gave 27-60 mL trough-FEV1 gains that missed the sponsor's 50 mL decision bar and the drug was dropped; inhaled AZD7624 (2018) and acumapimod (2019) then failed their primaries too.
efficacy.quote: However, none of the 5 doses of PH-797804 met the predefined decision criteria for improvement over placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 at Week 12.
efficacy.confidence_note: EudraCT results for NCT01543919 first published 2015-07-11 (tier 3); the ICS/LABA-background trial NCT01321463 synopsis (EudraCT 2010-024219-15, 2016-06-02) gave 27 mL with posterior probability 0.104 of a 50 mL gain. Point estimates were positive with CIs excluding zero, so the call inherits the checker's open rule question (contra vs same + partial); it follows the draft's contra reading for consistency. Later member failures (Patel 2018 AZD7624 HR 1.39; Strâmbu 2019 acumapimod Day-10 FEV1 p=0.082) keep the track contra and are not separate entries.
efficacy.judgement: Dose/efficacy table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': the smoke model predicted disease benefit from p38 inhibition and the first member to reach adequately powered 12-week trials failed its bar and was dropped. One drug's contra beats another's same on the track. Paired comparison with Medicherla 2008 as model side; no source ever stated this comparison, which is why the whole track is hatched.

patient_trials.quote: However, none of the 5 doses of PH-797804 met the predefined decision criteria for improvement over placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 at Week 12.

However, PH-797804 did not meet the second predefined decision criteria of a >0.50 posterior probability of a ≥0.050 L change from Baseline in trough FEV1 over placebo at Week 12 (estimated posterior probability of 0.104).

efficacy.reason: Smoke-model promise not borne out in COPD

efficacy.model: Ex-vivo COPD-patient alveolar macrophages, LPS cytokine release (SB239063, SD-282; later AZD7624)
efficacy.note: Macrophages from smokers and emphysema patients: sibling p38 inhibitors cut LPS-induced TNF-alpha regardless of disease status, which the authors read as a therapeutic lead for COPD.
efficacy.quote: Thus, inhibition of macrophage cytokine production may have therapeutic benefit.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Br J Pharmacol 149:393, PMC1978438); same source and quote as the track's engagement opening, here opening the efficacy cell at the track's first use.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the efficacy cell of the existing ex-vivo COPD-macrophage track at its first use (2006); sibling drugs only, so product_in_model false.

efficacy.model: Ex-vivo COPD-patient alveolar macrophages, LPS cytokine release (SB239063, SD-282; later AZD7624)
efficacy.note: Armstrong 2011 found sibling BIRB-796 synergised with dexamethasone in COPD alveolar macrophages; oral PH-797804 6 mg added to salmeterol/fluticasone (NCT01321463) gave +27 mL trough FEV1 over placebo at 12 weeks, missing Pfizer's decision bar.
efficacy.short: Add-on to ICS/LABA: +27 mL, bar missed
efficacy.quote: However, PH-797804 did not meet the second predefined decision criteria of a >0.50 posterior probability of a ≥0.050 L change from Baseline in trough FEV1 over placebo at Week 12 (estimated posterior probability of 0.104).
efficacy.confidence_note: Pfizer public-disclosure synopsis attached to EudraCT 2010-024219-15 (published 2016-06-02), as cited in the draft's rodent-track efficacy entry 3; first criterion (posterior probability >0.5 of any gain) met at 0.927. The status shares rule question 1 (below-bar positive primary, then abandoned).
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra on the same basis as the draft's 2015 rodent-track entry: a member drug run as add-on to a corticosteroid, the exact setting Armstrong 2011 predicts, gave a sub-MCID 27 mL gain that failed the sponsor's bar and ended the programme. Class level, no stated comparison.
efficacy.reason: Predicted steroid add-on benefit did not appear

safety.model: Rat and cynomolgus endotoxin-induced TNF-alpha PD model (PH-797804)
safety.note: Hope 2009 published PD only, no toxicology or margin; PH-797804's dose-related adverse-event discontinuations in the 12-week COPD trials (drug-related 6.9% vs 2.7%) have no stated animal prediction to compare.
safety.short: No published tox margin to compare
safety.quote: After oral dosing, PH-797804 effectively inhibits acute inflammatory responses induced by systemically administered endotoxin in both rat and cynomolgus monkeys.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Clinical tolerability: MacNee 2013 reports PH-797804 'well tolerated at all doses studied' at 6 weeks; the Pfizer synopsis for NCT01321463 (EudraCT 2010-024219-15) lists discontinuations for drug-related adverse events in 13/189 on 6 mg vs 5/187 on placebo, and EudraCT 2011-005864-11 shows AE discontinuations rising to 19/182 at 6 mg. No NDA exists, so no FDA non-clinical review was available.
safety.judgement: Untested, not contra: the only published model for PH-797804 made no safety statement, and a PD model's silence on rash, dizziness or liver signals is not a prediction. The class's known oral p38 harms (hepatic, skin) were learned in rheumatoid arthritis trials of other inhibitors and would be imported evidence from another indication, not a model prediction, so they are not scored.

safety.model: AstraZeneca human alveolar-macrophage/whole-blood LPS-TNF potency model with rat inhaled lung PK (AZD7624)
safety.note: Rat inhaled dosing gave 5x the lung exposure of IV, predicting lung effect without systemic p38 harm; in volunteers unbound plasma stayed at 0.3 nM, below the cell potencies, with no serious adverse events.
safety.short: Inhaled route kept systemic exposure sub-pharmacologic
safety.quote: This demonstrates that AZD7624 can achieve significant local lung pharmacodynamic effects with concomitant sub-pharmacological systemic exposure.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (JPET 365:567); the stated prediction is a platform one (inhaled delivery avoids systemic p38-inhibitor toxicity) tested in healthy volunteers. In the 12-week COPD trial (Patel 2018, full text) serious adverse events were 11/108 vs 11/105 and the drug was 'well tolerated', although most AE categories (COPD, dyspnoea, cough) were more frequent on AZD7624.
safety.judgement: Scored same because the source itself compares the rat lung:systemic exposure prediction with the human unbound plasma level and PD (comparison_stated true), and the predicted absence of systemic pharmacology held. Direction only: the model gave a ratio, not a human exposure. The respiratory AE excess in COPD patients is not a systemic harm and is not what the model predicted about, so it is noted, not scored.
safety.magnitude_basis: unbound plasma 0.3 nM vs cell pIC50u 8.4-9.0; the rat gave a lung:IV exposure ratio, not a human exposure

safety.model: Mouse H1N1 influenza infection model dosed with BCT197 (acumapimod) at clinically relevant exposure (Novartis)
safety.note: Novartis dosed BALB/c mice infected with H1N1 PR8 with BCT197 from 24 h post-infection: less weight loss, better survival and no impaired viral control at AECOPD-trial-relevant concentrations; benefit lost at higher doses.
safety.short: Mouse flu model: no impaired viral control predicted
safety.quote: This is encouraging given that the use of innate inflammatory pathway inhibitors may raise concerns of negative effects on infection regulation.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (J Med Microbiol 67:452, PMID 29458547, epub 2018-01-24); full text paywalled (journal page returned a bot check). The abstract states the mouse concentrations were chosen to match those in the AECOPD trials, and that at higher BCT197 concentrations the benefit was reduced. Authors are all Novartis (NIBR Emeryville/Cambridge, Novartis Pharmaceuticals).
safety.judgement: Opens a separate animal track: an influenza-infection model asks whether p38 inhibition during a viral lung infection impairs host defence, a different model and a different prediction from the LPS neutrophilia, endotoxin TNF and smoke-inflammation systems. Opened at its public first use (2018); the experiments were run earlier but the abstract does not date them. Only the safety cell is scored: the paper frames its result as an infection-regulation question, and mouse survival is not the AECOPD trials' FEV1 endpoint.

safety.model: Mouse H1N1 influenza infection model dosed with BCT197 (acumapimod) at clinically relevant exposure (Novartis)
safety.note: Novartis' own AECOPD trial (NCT01332097, 2011-2013) had already found acumapimod well tolerated when the Novartis mouse study appeared; the no-impaired-infection prediction reproduces that record, so retro, not same.
safety.short: Reproduces tolerability already in sponsor's hands
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (COPD 16:344, PMID 31682162, epub 2019-11-04); the abstract gives no infection-AE counts, so 'well tolerated' is read as absence of an infection-control signal, which is thin. NCT01332097 results were submitted 2017-10-25 and posted 2023-03-21. The later AETHER registry record (NCT02700919, posted 2020-11-30, 282 patients) shows serious pneumonia 1/92, 3/96, 2/91 and serious viral infection 0/92, 1/96, 0/91 for high dose, low dose and placebo, i.e. no infection excess; it post-dates this entry and changes no status.
safety.reason: No infection harm in acumapimod AECOPD trials
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the Novartis authors ran a Novartis drug in the model after Novartis' AECOPD trial had completed (May 2013), so the clinic already held the tolerability answer; decision 10 makes a reproduced human result 'retro', never 'same'. Paired comparison (comparison_stated false): model side Growcott 2018, patient side Strâmbu 2019. Direction only: mouse survival and viral titre are not commensurable with patient AE rates. The model also stated the benefit was lost at higher concentrations; no trial dosed above 75 mg, so that part is untested. If the checker reads the model's run date as before the 2013 trial, this becomes 'same'.
safety.magnitude_basis: absence of an infection-related harm: mouse survival/viral control vs patient tolerability; not commensurable
